title: POC acceptance criteria & benchmark runbook walkthrough
summary: Walkthrough and sign-off of POC acceptance thresholds, benchmark runbook, dataset sizing, and reporting format. Agreed on go/no-go matrix: latency p95, throughput steady-state, hallucination/factuality thresholds on labeled testset, and cost per 100k tokens. Timeline: 2-week benchmark window plus 3-day analysis. Action owners and next steps captured.
next_steps: Redwood to run baseline benchmark on dedicated test cluster (Marcos) by 2025-09-10
Customer to provide 1k labeled prompts + expected outputs by 2025-09-05
Exchange runbook and measurement dashboard link; Lila to share pricing delta for dedicated vs hosted by 2025-09-06
action_items: Marcos Chen: run cold+warm KV-cache benchmark and upload results (due 2025-09-10)
Priya Nair: deliver labeled acceptance prompt set and golden responses (due 2025-09-05)
Lila Porter: send final runbook PDF, CSV schema and RBAC access for dashboard (due 2025-09-06)
Omar Hassan: provision sample VPC peering for private run on staging infra (due 2025-09-08)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-03 15:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Lila P. (Redwood AE), Marcos C. (Redwood SE), Avery G. (Redwood Solutions), Priya N., Omar H., Rae K. (Cardea Health)

[00:00] Lila (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I know we're tight on time, we'll focus on the acceptance criteria and the runbook itself. Quick check — did everyone get the draft runbook?
[00:08] Priya: Yes got it, skimmed, looks good. We'll need to validate the metrics and also make sure there are tests that exercise our long-form summaries.
[00:14] Marcos (SE): Cool. I put together three benchmark modes in the runbook: cold-start (no KV cache), warm-cache steady-state, and peak-concurrency stress. For each we capture p50/p95/p99 for latency, tokens-per-second, and GPU utilization.
[00:28] Omar: For Cardea our primary success metric is accuracy/factuality on the patient-safety prompts — we need hallucination rate < 2% on the labeled set and F1 > 0.88 on extraction tasks. Is that something you can operationalize?
[00:39] Marcos: Yes we can compute hallucination rate by comparing generated output to your golden responses — we'll need a labeled set. We'll instrument an automated scorer (levenshtein+rule heuristics + human spot checks). Note — auto transcriber sometimes calls KV as K V cache, ignore that.
[00:50] Rae: A quick note on distribution — our prompts are long, median 1,200 tokens, 90th perc ~4k. Does your runtime handle that gracefully?
[01:01] Avery: Yep, we tested with long-seq quantized configs. We'll include sequence-length buckets in the report: short (<512), medium (512-2k), long (2k-6k). We'll show per-bucket p95 and also memory pressure.
[01:18] Priya: Ok back to thresholds — Listing what we think should be go/no-go: latency p95 < 400ms for short prompts, < 1,200ms for medium, < 3,500ms for long in warm cache; throughput should support sustained 50 concurrent requests with <10% error rate; hallucination <2%; F1 extraction >0.88; 95% of embedding cosine similarity recall >0.92 for retrieval tasks. Thoughts?
[01:38] Lila: Those are reasonable, we typically recommend slightly looser thresholds on the first run, then tightened on canary rollout. But for POC acceptance it's fair to require these if you're planning to go to dedicated after. We can also show cost-per-100k tokens to compare hosted vs dedicated.
[01:55] Omar: Cost is huge for us. We need a clear unit economics line in the report. If dedicated is 30% cheaper but adds complexity, stakeholders will want the numbers.
[02:05] Marcos: We'll compute effective $/100k output tokens under the two configs and include amortized GPU uptime. We'll also include a runbook section on batching and quant settings used for each run.
[02:15] Priya: On evaluation, please be explicit about what counts as a pass: e.g., hallucination measured only on the labeled set, not inferred from heuristics. And include the raw outputs in CSV.
[02:25] Marcos: Yep CSV schema: prompt_id, prompt_text (truncated), model_variant, run_mode, latency_ms_p50, latency_ms_p95, latency_ms_p99, tokens_out, gpu_util_pct, hallucination_flag (0/1), extraction_f1, cost_usd_estimate. We'll share schema in the runbook.
[02:46] Lila: Great, that matches what stakeholders asked. We'll also attach a short executive summary template with go/no-go matrix and a single page of recommended next steps.
[02:55] Rae: About the test harness: we prefer you run on our staging infra for a representative network path. Omar can provision VPC peering. If that's not possible, Redwood's dedicated test cluster is acceptable but we need to document delta to production.
[03:12] Omar: I'm on it, I'll open a ticket with infra and give read-only peering to the test account. Timing depends on our change window but I can try to have it by Friday.
[03:20] Marcos: If VPC peering is delayed, we'll run on dedicated test and then re-run the critical long-seq jobs once peering exists. We will tag runs as "staging-peered" vs "hosted-dedicated" — both will be in the final CSV.
[03:34] Priya: For the labeled set size — do you need a large test corpus? We can provide 1k prompts initially but can stretch to 3k if needed.
[03:41] Marcos: 1k is a good start — statistically useful across buckets. For hallucination detection and extraction metrics, 1k with balanced examples across short/med/long should be fine. If you can provide 3k we'll subsample for latency runs to save cost.
[03:57] Lila: Let's lock that: Cardea will provide 1,000 labeled prompts + 200 edge-case prompts by 2025-09-05. Redwood will run baseline (cold/warm/stress) and upload raw CSVs by 2025-09-10. We'll have a go/no-go review 2025-09-14.
[04:13] Rae: Sounds good. A question on measurement: for hallucination what exact heuristic do you use? We prefer human adjudication for a 10% sample to validate auto labels.
[04:22] Marcos: Agreed. Our auto-hallucination flag uses string overlap + entity mismatch rules; we'll run that then sample 10% for human adjudication and report both numbers. We'll also include inter-annotator stats if you want.
[04:35] Omar: How will you handle rate limiting during stress tests — we want to mimic production client behavior: bursts up to 200 concurrent for 30s then back to steady 50.
[04:45] Marcos: The runbook defines a synthetic traffic profile: 0-30s ramp, 30-60s sustain at target concurrency, 30s spike, repeat 20 cycles. We'll include error-rate and retry behavior.
[04:56] Lila: One more item — reporting format. You asked for raw CSVs and an executive dashboard. We'll supply a Grafana snapshot link and a zipped CSV bundle. The go/no-go will be summarized in a one-page matrix: pass/fail per metric with comments.
[05:11] Priya: For the matrix, can you use green/yellow/red thresholds and include severity? E.g., red = immediate fail, yellow = mitigation plan required before production.
[05:21] Lila: Yes we'll adopt that. We'll publish thresholds and the exact definition in the runbook so there's no ambiguity.
[05:28] Rae: On the subject of models — which model variants will you test? We prefer smallest accurate variant to reduce cost.
[05:34] Marcos: We'll test three: base open model (quantized), Redwood-verified medium variant, and the production tuned variant (if you allow). We'll include BLEU-like scores for summarization and custom metrics for extraction. Note: model names sometimes get patched in transcripts — we'll send an appendix of tested variants.
[05:50] Omar: Any security controls during the runs? We need audit logs and encrypted-at-rest access for the golden set.
[05:56] Avery: We'll enable KMS-backed storage for artifacts and SSO-based access to the dashboard. We'll also create an audit bucket and log entries for each run. We'll include a short security checklist in the runbook.
[06:08] Priya: Great. I want to ensure the acceptance criteria include a manual sign-off step from product after we review the raw outputs.
[06:15] Lila: Absolutely — go/no-go is not purely numeric. We'll present the matrix, the raw CSV and 10 human-checked examples; product will have final sign-off within 48 hours of report delivery.
[06:25] Marcos: Quick clarification on sampling for human checks — we'll pick stratified samples across sequence-length buckets and error classes. Good to capture edge cases.
[06:34] Omar: Ok timeline recap?
[06:36] Lila: Cardea deliver labeled set by 2025-09-05; Redwood baseline run results by 2025-09-10; analysis and dashboard by 2025-09-12; go/no-go review on 2025-09-14. Also pricing delta and runbook PDF to be shared by 2025-09-06.
[06:51] Rae: Sounds tight but doable. One more ask — please include the raw latency histograms per run, not just percentiles.
[06:58] Marcos: Will do. We'll include histogram PNGs and histogram CSVs.
[07:04] Priya: I have one last concern — what if the POC meets metrics but shows regression on a small set of privacy-sensitive prompts? Do we have a remediation path?
[07:13] Lila: If there's a localized regression we'll discuss targeted model-variant rollbacks and canarying strategies. We'll also provide a mitigation plan (prompt engineering, post-processing filters). We'll flag severity in the executive matrix.
[07:26] Omar: Ok, thanks. Anything else?
[07:29] Lila: No — thanks everyone. We'll email runbook v1 final and calendar for 9/14 review.
[07:36] Priya: Thanks all.

Meeting ended at 15:52 UTC
file_notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts and generic speaker labels consistent with Fireflies exports. Report schema and runbook items should be considered the authoritative POC artifacts.
